data.title: blog/: build the /blog site from BRANDING.md — home, post pages, posting workflow

data.to:
Build the /blog sub-site from blog/BRANDING.md (written in FA-31).

WHY: The user wants a place to publish their writing at forrestalmasi.com/blog, styled per the Web 2.0 brief.

DELIVERABLE:
- blog/index.html — blog home: masthead, post list with excerpts and permalinks, sidebar, footer.
- blog/style.css — separate stylesheet, per the CLAUDE.md sub-site authoring contract.
- Individual post pages plus a documented way to add a new post without a build step.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Follow the sub-site authoring contract in CLAUDE.md (ids prefixed with the site name, relative url() for local assets, no external requests unless the brief names a font, no horizontal scroll, full-bleed background) so the folder could be mapped into a viewport bucket later if wanted.
- NOT mapped in sites.config.json and the root index.html is NOT rebuilt for this task — /blog is a standalone destination. Do not hand-edit root index.html.
- Everything the brief specifies must actually appear in the page.

CONTENT: Do not fabricate opinions or biography in the user's voice. Ship a genuine first "Hello world"-style post about starting the blog plus a copy-to-write post template; the user supplies the real writing.

data.body: Plan written (574 lines). Files: blog/{index,archive}.html, blog/style.css, blog/posts/2026-09-03-hello-world.html, blog/posts/_template.html, blog/feed.xml, blog/README.md. No blog/script.js and no Search module — a client-side filter over a one-post list is a dead widget by the brief's rule 2, so the site ships zero JS. Key decisions: (1) NOT noindex — sibling folders carry noindex because build.js inlines their bodies into the root page, making the standalone copy a duplicate; /blog is not in sites.config.json, its content is unique, and it exists to be read, so index.html/archive.html/posts get canonical + no robots meta, while _template.html keeps noindex. (2) Exactly one real post, no placeholder entries — inventing entries is the dead-widget failure the brief forbids and the task forbids fabricating in the author's voice; the post is written long enough that the front-page excerpt + 'Continue reading' is a genuine excerpt, so the whole entry anatomy is exercised by one post. (3) url() tension resolved: verified the brief holds to zero url() everywhere it could have cheated (ground is gradients, chiclet is drawn, avatar is markup), so ONE stylesheet serves ./style.css and ../style.css; I made the avatar inline SVG rather than to kill the per-depth src, and both inline SVGs carry no internal ids so they can repeat in one document. (4) Sidebar modules made load-bearing concretely with a one-post corpus, incl. an absolute-threshold tag-cloud step table (1 post -> step 1) rather than a relative max. (5) Badge recipe goes on the truthful footer badge row, never a NEW/BETA sticker, which ages into a lie without a build step. (6) Yellow Fade made live by pointing every permalink at posts/.html#blog-entry-. Restated the FA-31 review finding at the top: style.css must never contain the string #site-blog.

Implementation complete. Files: blog/{index,archive}.html, blog/style.css, blog/posts/2026-09-03-hello-world.html, blog/posts/_template.html, blog/feed.xml, blog/README.md. No blog/script.js, no Search module, zero JS, zero assets.

COMMIT NOTE: I did not create the commit. While I was verifying, the user committed ac6fb3d 'no white space' at 13:23, which swept in all 7 blog/ files (byte-identical to my working tree) together with their own unrelated sites.config.json bucket remap and the .lattice files. I left it alone per the shared-worktree rule rather than amending or reverting a human commit, so there is no 'blog: ...' house-style message and no Co-Authored-By trailer on the blog work. Reviewer: diff ac6fb3d limited to blog/. Confirmed /blog is still NOT in sites.config.json and root index.html has no site-blog reference, so the out-of-scope constraints hold.

VERIFIED: grep style.css -> 0 'url(', 0 '#site-', 0 '@import|:is(|:where(', 0 '</style>', 0 position fixed/sticky, only radii 4/6/999px, only keyframe blog-yft. All 49 :root tokens the brief names in S2/S3/S4.6/S5 present and spelled as the brief spells them; every var() resolves; no dangling refs. Markup: no root-absolute href/src, no href='#', no <script>, no id outside the blog- prefix, no duplicate ids within any document, balanced nesting (HTMLParser), 0 dead links across all 4 pages incl. every fragment anchor. feed.xml parses. Rendered all pages in headless Chrome: layout math exact at >=940 (wrapper 940 = 12 + 620 + 28 + 268 + 12), masthead 110px with the wordmark above and tagline below the 50% hard stop, active tab connected, gloss/sheen/module/badge/chiclet/avatar/tag-well all render, full-bleed ground. At 320px (measured in an iframe, since headless Chrome clamps its window to 500) documentElement.scrollWidth == 320 on all three served pages: no horizontal scroll, nav wraps to two rows, sidebar below main. :target Yellow Fade fires on the post permalink; under --force-prefers-reduced-motion the entry arrives un-highlighted.

DECISIONS BEYOND THE PLAN: (1) .blog-well needed a home -- it cannot go on a blockquote or pre without violating 'no tint/radius/shadow on prose', so it wraps the tag cloud, which is chrome. (2) .blog-tag-3 'mix toward --link' is color-mix(in srgb, var(--link) 55%, var(--ink-soft)) rather than a new hex, so the palette stays closed to declared tokens; measures 5.8 on Alt Row, and degrades to --link if color-mix is unsupported. (3) --blue-lite is declared but never referenced: the only place the brief uses it is the tag-pill hover tint, which the brief writes literally as rgb(91 163 224 / 0.15); I kept the literal and annotated it. (4) Added .blog-post-nav CSS so the commented-out prev/next markup in _template.html is styled when someone uncuts it. (5) Wrapper is a single rounded, shadowed, overflow-hidden card; the white column has no side hairlines so the 916px content math lands exactly without a doubled edge.

CONTENT: One real post, no placeholders. Every sentence in the post, the tagline ('Writing by Forrest Almasi') and the About blurb is true by virtue of the page existing -- no opinions, biography, cadence promises or technical claims invented in the user's voice, and nothing captions the design. Blogroll is the four links verified in vhs/index.html only.

LEFT FOR THE USER: (a) the About blurb is a slot, marked with a <!-- blog:about-blurb --> comment in all 4 pages -- currently two true sentences, meant to be replaced; (b) the hello-world post is a replaceable stub, called out in blog/README.md, not in the post; (c) the post timestamp is the real authoring time, September 3 2026 at 1:14 pm, matching feed.xml's RFC-822 pubDate; (d) no prev/next nav exists with one post, by design, with the wiring rule documented in README and _template.

REVIEW (fresh context, cold read of git show ac6fb3d -- blog/, plus blog/BRANDING.md and the plan). Reviewed all 7 shipped files; sites.config.json in that commit is the user's own unrelated work and was not reviewed or touched.

VERDICT: PASS, with two fixes applied inline and committed as b5e0634 (blog/ only).

FIX 1 — real layout defect, found by rendering, not present in the implementer's own test matrix. .blog-main and .blog-sidebar were both `flex: 0 0 <fixed>`, so the 916px column system (620+28+268) was rigid while .blog-wrap is `min(100% - 24px, 940px)`. Between the 760px breakpoint and the 964px viewport at which the wrapper first reaches 940, the columns were wider than their container and .blog-wrap's `overflow: hidden` silently clipped the sidebar: measured in headless Chrome, at 768px the sidebar's right edge sat at x=940 while the content box ended at 756 — about 184px of the 268px sidebar invisible, i.e. only the left third of every module rendered. Same at 860 and at 940. The implementer verified 320px and >=940px and never probed the band between, and `overflow: hidden` masked it from the "no horizontal scroll" check (scrollWidth == viewport at every width, before and after). Fixed by making main the shrinking column (`flex: 1 1 620px`); the sidebar keeps its designed 268 throughout and the exact 940/620/28/268 math still lands at >=964. Re-measured across 320/375/600/760/768/860/940/964/1440 on all three real pages: sidebar within the content box everywhere, no clipping, no horizontal scroll.

FIX 2 — content honesty. Paragraph 4 of the hello-world post read "There is no comment system either, because a static site cannot serve one honestly." The trailing clause is a rationale asserted in Forrest's voice that is not true purely by virtue of the page existing (and static sites do serve third-party comment systems). Trimmed to "There is no comment system either." Not in the excerpt, so index.html and feed.xml were unaffected.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not taken from the impl report):
- style.css: 0 `url(`, 0 `#site-`, 0 `@import|:is(|:where(`, 0 position fixed/sticky, only radii 4/6/999px, only keyframe `blog-yft`. Palette hexes diffed against BRANDING.md §2 — all 23 colour/depth tokens match exactly, no drift. Every `var(--x)` in the sheet resolves to a declared token (script-checked); `--blue-lite` is declared-but-unused, which is correct — the brief writes its one use site as a literal.
- Both depths: parsed every href/src in all 4 pages and resolved it against the filesystem plus the target document's id set. Zero dead files and zero dead fragments on index/archive/post; the only unresolvable links are the `[tag]`/`[YYYY-MM-DD]` placeholders in _template.html, by design. `./style.css` vs `../style.css`, `./feed.xml` vs `../feed.xml`, nav, permalinks, tag pills, archive months and the post's own self-permalink are all correct at their depth.
- Zero `<script>` in any shipped page (the two hits are code samples in README.md and BRANDING.md). Zero external requests: no webfont, no @import, no CDN, no remote image, no analytics. The only external URLs are the four blogroll anchors, the OG/Twitter meta and feed.xml absolutes. `http://` on og:image with an `og:image:secure_url` beside it matches the house block in template.html and memphis/index.html.
- Ids: every id on every page is `blog-`-prefixed; zero duplicates within any single document (HTMLParser-checked per file). No `id="site-blog"`, no `href="#"`.
- feed.xml: well-formed; RSS 2.0 channel has title/link/description/language/lastBuildDate; the item has title/link/description/pubDate/guid. pubDate "Thu, 03 Sep 2026 13:14:28 -0400" is RFC-822 and 2026-09-03 is genuinely a Thursday. The link and guid resolve to a real shipped file and a real id on it, at the real domain.
- Cross-page consistency (script-diffed after normalising ./ vs ../): sidebar block byte-identical across index/archive/post — _template differs only in its bracketed placeholders. Masthead identical on all 4. Nav differs only in which tab carries blog-tab-on/aria-current, which is correct (and no tab is lit on a post page, per plan). Footer identical on index/archive; post and template both add a "Blog" link to the colophon, consistent with each other. No rot found.
- README.md workflow walked step by step against the real tree: the five steps, the id shapes, the tag-cloud table, the RFC-822 skeleton, the date/time format, the prev/next rule, the no-url()/no-#site-blog rules, the registry-function shape, the stub note and the BRANDING.md pointer are all present and all accurate. Step 5's "the sidebar in every page" honestly names index + archive + _template + every post rather than pretending five files is forever.
- Rendered over file:// and over http: all three pages render correctly, styles load at both depths, ground is full-bleed, badge row and colophon present, layout math exact at >=964. `.blog-entry:target` computes `animation-name: blog-yft, 1.2s` when reached by permalink, and collapses to 0.01ms under --force-prefers-reduced-motion.
- Load-bearing widget rule holds: all five modules do something real (About is the nav's About target with a real outbound link, Subscribe points at a feed whose newest item is the newest post, both tag pills and the archive month resolve to real anchors, the blogroll is four verified links). No Search module, no prev/next stub, no NEW/BETA sticker.
- Content honesty: after fix 2, every remaining sentence in the post, the tagline and the About blurb is true by construction. No invented opinion, biography, employment, cadence or technical claim. Nothing anywhere captions the design (grepped copy, alt text and comments for web 2.0 / retro / throwback / nostalgia / 2006).
- Out of scope confirmed untouched: sites.config.json has no blog entry, root index.html has no site-blog reference, no blog/script.js exists.

NOTES, no action needed: (a) BRANDING.md §5 says the content column carries a 1px border; the implementer dropped the side hairlines so 916 lands exactly. That is the right call — a border-box wrapper with a border makes 916 impossible — but the brief and the sheet now disagree on one line, so if anyone later re-reads §5 as normative, this is the known divergence. (b) The post's last paragraph says "Right now there is one post"; that sentence ages the moment post 2 ships. README already calls the post a replaceable stub, so it is covered, but it is the one line in the corpus with a shelf life.
